rq1_question: How faithfully does the current ProvenLattice Graph Fabric represent and resolve the evaluated C/C++ structural relations under the frozen V1 benchmark?

verdict.summary: Within the frozen V1 benchmark, ProvenLattice V0.2 usually selects the correct semantic target when it resolves an evaluable C/C++ CALLS or IMPORTS relation, but population-level fidelity is substantially limited by resolution coverage, especially CALLS in high-weight nonresolved strata.

positive_basis: independent blinded annotation across multiple batches

weighted_interpretation.explanation: The descriptive sample is stratified and intentionally balanced across repository, relation, and resolved/nonresolved strata. Population weighting restores frozen population shares, so it is dominated by large nonresolved strata rather than by the sample allocation.

non_equivalences: candidate target absent is not resolver selected wrong candidate
correct candidate present but unresolved is not candidate-generation failure
Gold ABSENT but system resolves is not missed resolution

supported: The frozen scoring-state counts and metrics reported in this artifact.
Resolved semantic targets are usually correct in both the descriptive sample and weighted estimates.
Coverage is the primary measured limitation relative to wrong-target selection.
The three failure mechanisms are distinct and should not be collapsed into resolver errors.
C/C++ REFERENCES population is zero and REFERENCES fidelity cannot be estimated in V1.
supported_with_scope_qualifier: Current V0.2 usually resolves evaluated C/C++ CALLS and IMPORTS to the correct semantic target in this frozen three-repository benchmark.
IMPORTS is strong within this benchmark.
CALLS is the dominant fidelity limitation within this benchmark.
Population-weighted fidelity is more coverage-limited than the descriptive sample view.
not_supported: ProvenLattice has high graph fidelity in general.
ProvenLattice outperforms Joern, SCIP, or CodeGraphContext.
ProvenLattice works at one-million- or 10M-LOC fidelity.
The Graph Fidelity problem is solved.
The unweighted sample directly represents the deployment population.

threats_and_limitations: dependence on frozen stratified sampling and weights
next_evidence_required: freeze a C/C++ REFERENCES population before estimating REFERENCES fidelity
replicate on additional repositories and relation populations
run an independently frozen post-repair evaluation before claiming improvement
add external-system baselines before comparative claims
validate fidelity at substantially larger graph scales before scale claims

milestone_recommendation.wording: P0 Graph Fidelity Qualification V1 may be frozen as a completed QUALIFIED research milestone; this closes the bounded evidence milestone, not the Graph Fidelity problem.
